_comment: Adapt this file to the real Copilot CLI in the target environment. Run `copilot --help` and fix the `command`, `models`, and `args` sections. No JS changes should be needed.
_models_comment: Checked 2026-08-04 on a Copilot 'individual'/free-limited account: `--model <name>` rejected every explicit value tried, including the account's own auto-selected models by display name ('gpt-5-mini', 'claude-haiku-4.5' both got 'Error: Model "..." from --model flag is not available.'). Root cause found via `gh api /copilot_internal/user`: that account's `premium_interactions.entitlement` was 0 — the free plan simply has no quota for premium models, independent of naming. `can_upgrade_plan: true` was set. This config is written for a Copilot Pro (or higher) account where that entitlement is nonzero. UNVERIFIED on Pro: re-run `gh api /copilot_internal/user --jq .quota_snapshots.premium_interactions` after upgrading to confirm entitlement > 0, then test one `codex` call with an explicit model before trusting this table for real work.

args._comment: Each entry is an argv template. {{var}} is substituted. An empty array disables that argument entirely.

_effort_comment: Verified 2026-08-03 against copilot 1.0.77: `--effort, --reasoning-effort <level>` is a real flag (choices from --help: none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max). ALSO verified 2026-08-04: passing --effort together with --model auto fails outright — 'Error: Model "auto" does not support reasoning effort configuration'. Effort is a per-model setting; it only works alongside an explicit model (see the `models` map above), which on this account requires the Pro-plan premium_interactions entitlement described in _models_comment. On a free-tier account, leave `model` unset/auto and treat this whole `effort` block as inert.
_sessionIdPattern_comment: Verified 2026-08-03 against copilot 1.0.77: text output prints the resume hint to stderr as '--resume=<id>'; --output-format json (not currently enabled — see args.extra) would print it as "sessionId":"<id>" in a stdout result line instead. This pattern matches either.
